output.brief:
The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% looks like ordinary week-to-week variation. Over the previous 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354% with a normal upper edge of 0.482%. Three past weeks were higher than this one, and the ones investigated turned up no fault. The burn rate is 0.82x, well under the 2x paging threshold. The dashboard counts match raw logs, so the rise is not a counting artefact. Booking completion and support complaints did not change.

The "new pods error twice as often" finding is a warm-up effect. New pods start with an empty cache and time out against the database. The same gap showed up in every one of the last five rollouts, including a config-only redeploy, so it doesn't implicate v4.18. It adds only 10–20 errors per rollout.

I'm fairly confident, though not certain, that v4.18 is not the cause. I did not test the replica move or partner-sync traffic, so those stay open.

What to do: don't roll back, don't move the replica back, and don't mute alerting. Record the week as normal and run the standard check on the following week. If the next week breaches the band, investigate then.
